source: scripts/check_content.py, `read_table`: "with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as fh: reader = csv.reader(fh)" and the blank-line rule "if not row or (len(row) == 1 and row[0].strip() == ""): continue  # blank line". `expected` is what Python's csv module yields through that path: the UTF-8 BOM dropped by utf-8-sig, blank and whitespace-only lines skipped, every other line a row of cells. A case whose text makes csv.reader raise is written "error"; Python accepts every text here, so none uses it.
notes: The frontend reader (frontend/src/content/csv.ts) differs on two cases today: a quoted newline, which it splits at the physical line, and a line starting with "#", which it skips instead of reading as a row. FORMATS.md says nothing about comment lines.

cases.name: quoted comma stays in one cell
doubled quote reads as one quote
quoted newline stays in one cell
line starting with # is a row
